partners.mechanism_chain: KCNQ2 (HGNC:6247) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal action potential propagation (GO:0001506); Neuronal action potential propagation (GO:0001506) —LEADS_TO→ seizures (HP:0001250); SCN3B (HGNC:10597) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal action potential propagation (GO:0001506); Neuronal action potential propagation (GO:0001506) —LEADS_TO→ Brugada syndrome (HP:0011674). Both KCNQ2 (causative for BFNS1) and SCN3B (causative for BrS7) are critical components of voltage-gated potassium and sodium channels, respectively, which are essential for neuronal excitability and cardiac action potential propagation. Haploinsufficiency of either gene disrupts the normal function of these ion channels, leading to altered neuronal firing patterns and cardiac electrical activity, ultimately manifesting as seizures and Brugada syndrome, respectively. The convergence is on the shared pathway of neuronal action potential propagation, which is fundamental to both neurological and cardiac function.
